# 2 Kings Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 228r–228v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_007_page_001.jpg, 2KI_007_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the LORD: 'Tomorrow about this time, a seah of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.'"

**2** Then the officer on whose arm the king was leaning answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could this thing be?" Elisha said, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."

**3** Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the city gate, and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

**4** If we say, 'Let us enter the city,' the famine is in the city and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we die also. So now, come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they spare us, we shall live; if they kill us, we shall but die."

**5** So they arose at twilight to go to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the edge of the camp, behold, there was no one there.

**6** For the Lord had caused the army of the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots and horses — the sound of a great army — so that they said to one another, "The king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us."

**7** So they fled in the twilight, abandoning their tents, their horses, and their donkeys — leaving the camp just as it was — and fled for their lives.

**8** When these lepers came to the edge of the camp, they entered a tent, ate and drank, and carried off silver, gold, and garments, and went and hid them. Then they came back and entered another tent, and carried off more and went and hid it.

**9** Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, punishment will overtake us. Come now, let us go and tell the king's household."

**10** So they went and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, "We went to the camp of the Arameans, and behold, there was no one there — not a sound of anyone — only the horses tied and the donkeys tied and the tents just as they were."

**11** The gatekeepers called out, and it was told within the king's household.

**12** The king arose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country, thinking, 'When they come out of the city, we shall take them alive and get into the city.'"

**13** One of his servants answered, "Let some men take five of the remaining horses — those that are left will fare like the whole multitude of Israel who are already perishing — and let us send and see."

**14** So they took two horse-drawn chariots, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, "Go and see."

**15** They followed them as far as the Jordan, and behold, the whole way was littered with garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.

**16** Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a seah of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

**17** Now the king had appointed the officer on whose arm he leaned to have charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died — just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.

**18** For when the man of God had said to the king, "Two seahs of barley shall be sold for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria,"

**19** the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD should make windows in heaven, could such a thing be?" And Elisha had said, "You shall see it with your own eyes, but you shall not eat of it."

**20** And so it happened to him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 2 — "windows in heaven":** The Hebrew *arubbot ba-shamayim* echoes Genesis 7:11 (the flood) and Malachi 3:10 (blessing poured out). The officer uses flood imagery sarcastically — even divine intervention could not produce such abundance. His punishment fits his doubt: he will witness the miracle but die before tasting it.

**Verse 6 — "kings of the Hittites":** The reference is to the Neo-Hittite states of northern Syria (Carchemish, Hamath, etc.), not the ancient Anatolian Hittites. A coalition of Hittite and Egyptian forces would represent a strategic nightmare for Aram — enemies on both flanks.

**Verse 9 — "a day of good news":** Hebrew *yom besorah* — the root *b-s-r* is the same word that yields the concept of gospel (*euangelion*) in later Jewish and Christian usage. The irony is exquisite: the gospel is first proclaimed by lepers — the most marginal people in Israelite society.

**Verse 13 — A textual difficulty:** The Hebrew of v.13 is notoriously difficult, with apparent repetition. The servant's argument is essentially: "The horses left in the city are going to die anyway, like the rest of Israel — we might as well risk them on a scouting mission."

*— LOGOS*
